title: Reconstruction Estimating Guideline: Pricing a Removed Line by Who Priced the Work
content:
When a deductive change order removes scope from a Reconstruction contract, the removed line — the change-order part of the removal, that is the share of the quantity written on the deductive proposal that signed change orders of that scope code other than deductive ones added, less what signed deductive change orders of that scope code already removed — follows who priced the removed work.

**Guideline.**

1. **Carrier-priced scope.** On an insurance-claim contract where the signed insurance-scope change order of the removed scope code with the highest change order number names a supplement the carrier approved, as much of the change-order part as the signed insurance-scope change orders of that scope code added is credited at the carrier's approved unit price taken from that change order, which is the amount the carrier approved on the supplement it names divided by the quantity written on it, and the rest of the change-order part at the tier's rate for the scope code, or, for a scope code that has no tier rate, the unit price written on the proposal. The carrier's approval is the one recorded for that supplement on the claim file kept under Insurance Claim Services.
2. **Owner selection lines.** Otherwise, for a flooring upgrade, cabinet upgrade or fixture upgrade line, the change-order part is credited at the owner's selected unit price written on the proposal less the tier's selection allowance for that line (flooring allowance per square foot, cabinet allowance per linear foot, fixture allowance per fixture).
3. **Every other line.** The change-order part is credited at the tier's rate for the scope code, or, for a scope code that has no tier rate, the unit price written on the proposal.

## Which case applies

| Contract funding | Signed insurance-scope change order of that scope code with the highest number names a carrier-approved supplement | Scope code | Removed line |
|---|---|---|---|
| insurance claim | yes | any | carrier-added share at the carrier's unit price, the rest at the tier rate (or written price) |
| insurance claim | no such change order, or its supplement not approved | flooring, cabinet or fixture upgrade | change-order part at selected price less allowance |
| self-pay | any | flooring, cabinet or fixture upgrade | change-order part at selected price less allowance |
| any, outside the first case | — | any other | change-order part at the tier rate (or written price) |

## Worked case (hypothetical figures)

On an insurance-claim contract, the signed insurance-scope drywall change orders added 180 square feet; the one with the highest number was written for 120 square feet and names a supplement the carrier approved at $480.00, so the carrier's unit price is $4.00 per square foot. A deductive proposal's change-order part of drywall is 230 square feet (the rest of the added drywall came from an owner change order), and the drywall rate is assumed at $3.00. The removed line is 180 times $4.00, that is $720.00, plus 50 times $3.00, that is $150.00: $870.00.
